audit_findings.title: Post-close Helvoet financing makes the bridge and OE perimeter incoherent
audit_findings.magnitude: $103.0 million purchase price, equal to 25.8% of the $400.0 million base equity value; exact cash/debt funding split unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds June 30 cash and uses June 30 debt even though the acquisition closed July 1, while OE excludes Helvoet earnings and acquisition-financing interest.
audit_findings.evidence: In July 2026, the Company paid a purchase price of approximately 90.0 million Euro, or approximately $103.0 million which was funded with a combination of the Company’s cash and existing lines of credit.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possibility. The stale cash balance can overstate value, while excluding Helvoet earnings can understate value; the net direction cannot be established. The transaction is large enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 1 opening purchase accounting, cash paid, debt drawn, acquired liabilities, working-capital adjustment, and financing terms; rerun either a fully pre-deal valuation or a coherent post-deal valuation including Helvoet OE and financing costs.

audit_findings.title: The FY2026 numerator may retain a material nonrecurring property-sale gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $15.0 million pre-tax, equal to 67.0% of FY2026 OE of $22.4 million and 67.9% of the $22.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the nonrecurring gain inflates FY2026 OE and the ten-year log-trend used to establish anchor OE.
audit_findings.evidence: On April 22, 2026, the Company completed the sale of the Tampa land and buildings recording a gain on sale of $15.0 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The sale gain is filed, but its retention in OE is unresolved. Its scale relative to both latest and anchor OE makes the issue reasonably capable of materially increasing intrinsic value. If the gain was already removed, no correction is required.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $15.0 million gain and associated tax effect through the FY2026 OE reconciliation and trend inputs, then rerun the anchor and all scenarios if any after-tax gain remains.

audit_findings.title: A large legacy withholding-tax charge may distort normalized OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.9 million total, including $7.6 million tied to prior-period dividends and $1.3 million tied to a fiscal-2026 China dividend; total equals 40.3% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Retaining legacy catch-up taxes depresses FY2026 OE and its fitted trend, while removing prospective recurring withholding leakage would inflate normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal year 2026, the Company recorded dividend withholding tax expense in Netherlands of $ 8.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that most of the charge concerns earlier dividends, but it does not establish the normalized recurring amount or how the valuation treated it. The charge is large enough relative to the $22.1 million anchor to materially affect value in either direction.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the $4.4 million Poland amount and the $4.5 million China amount, including interest and the $1.3 million current-year component, to OE; retain only a supportable recurring withholding burden and rerun the trend and scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Recurring receivables-financing costs could be lost through classification changes
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.862 million in FY2026 and $2.415 million in FY2025; the FY2026 amount equals 17.5% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Purging items classified as non-operating after FY2024 could add back recurring factoring and RPA costs in FY2025-FY2026 while leaving equivalent earlier costs deducted, overstating OE and its trend.
audit_findings.evidence: Prior to fiscal year 2025, factoring fees were recorded in Selling and Administrative Expenses on our Consolidated Statements of Income.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification change and fee amounts are demonstrated; an erroneous add-back is not. Because these are recurring financing costs and the FY2026 amount is substantial relative to anchor OE, inconsistent treatment could materially overstate intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Trace factoring fees and RPA discounts year by year through the OE reconciliation, ensure they remain deducted regardless of presentation, and rerun the trend and scenarios if FY2025 or FY2026 costs were purged.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded postemployment obligations are an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $9.2 million, or $0.36 per diluted share and 2.3% of the $400.0 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If future benefit payments are not captured in projected OE, the unfunded obligation should reduce the equity bridge; deducting it when payments are already reflected would double count the claim.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 30, 2026, total obligations under these plans were $ 9.2 million of which $ 8.3 million were long term and $ 0.9 million were short term.
audit_findings.explanation: Even a full, tax-unadjusted $9.2 million bridge deduction would reduce base value only from $15.69 to approximately $15.33 per share, still far below the $25.03 market price. It therefore does not change the valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether projected OE includes expected benefit payments; if not, deduct the appropriately tax-adjusted obligation in the next rerun while avoiding double counting periodic benefit expense.

audit_findings.title: The fully diluted denominator remains a disclosed lower bound
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; disclosed FY2024-FY2026 grants total 70,867 units, equal to 0.28% of the 25.491878 million-share denominator, but aggregate outstanding units are not disclosed
audit_findings.mechanism: Omitted deferred share units understate fully diluted shares and therefore overstate value per share without changing aggregate equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: Deferred share units are participating securities and are payable in common stock in a lump sum or installments in accordance with deferral elections upon a director’s death, retirement, or termination of service with the Board.
audit_findings.explanation: The existence and stock settlement of deferred units are demonstrated, but the record does not provide the total outstanding balance or prior settlements. Recent grants alone appear small, but they cannot establish the scale of accumulated units since the plan began in 2016, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the Deferral Plan ledger or proxy reconciliation of all granted, settled, forfeited, and outstanding units; add the resulting outstanding stock-settled units to the diluted share ceiling and recompute per-share values.
